This would solve a real workflow gap for me.

I added a local profile switcher that rewrites agent model assignments in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (for example switching thinker/implementer/light agent groups between different models). The config file updates correctly, but the running OpenCode server keeps using the old cached models until restart.

I also tried the undocumented signal-based workaround and, in my setup, sending `SIGUSR2` to the running app/server just killed it instead of giving me a usable reload flow.

A supported `/reload` that re-reads global/project config and invalidates cached agent/config state would make model/profile switching usable without restarting the app.

## Root Cause Identified: Node.js v24 Silent Process Termination on Windows

This issue appears to be caused by a Node.js runtime bug, not an OpenCode logic error.

**Upstream bug**: [nodejs/node#62125](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/62125) — Node.js v24.13.x on Windows silently terminates child processes (including those spawned with \child_process.spawn()\) via \TerminateProcess()\ with **no JS exit handlers firing**, no diagnostic report, and no Event Log entry. The process simply vanishes.

### Why this matches the symptoms in this issue

- **Silent crashes with no error output** — exactly what \TerminateProcess()\ causes (bypasses all JS cleanup)
- **Node 24.13.0 in the reporter's environment** — the affected version range
- **Crash logs end abruptly** — the process is killed externally before it can write anything
- **Immediate successful restart** — the crash is caused by the runtime, not by application state corruption

### Independent verification

We independently encountered this exact bug while debugging a Chrome Native Messaging host chain on Windows. Our findings:

- A **bare \setInterval(() => {}, 1000)\ in a detached spawn dies in ~4-6 seconds** on v24.13.1 — zero I/O, zero business logic needed to reproduce
- **All exit handlers fail to fire**: \process.on('exit')\, \process.on('SIGTERM')\, \process.on('uncaughtException')\ — none trigger
- **Python equivalent survives indefinitely** under identical conditions — this is Node.js-specific
- **Downgrading to Node.js v22.22.2 LTS resolves the issue completely** (137+ seconds uptime verified)

### Workaround

`
# Use Node.js v22 LTS instead of v24
nvm install 22
nvm use 22
`

Or, if you need v24 for other reasons, spawn long-lived child processes using a v22 binary specifically:

\\\javascript
const nodeV22Path = 'path/to/node-v22.exe';
spawn(nodeV22Path, ['your-script.js'], { detached: true, stdio: 'ignore', windowsHide: true });
\\\

### Note for maintainers

OpenCode's own \ ash.ts\ and \cross-spawn-spawner.ts\ already correctly set \detached: false\ on Windows, which is good defensive coding. However, when users run via \
px\ on Node v24, the runtime-level bug can still affect the host process itself and any indirectly spawned children (e.g., MCP stdio transports, plugin processes).

Suggest adding a Node version check at startup that warns Windows users on v24.x about this upstream bug.
